description: US-08 Block and Unblock a Customer — Manual temporary block with a mandatory free-text reason, shown verbatim at the counter. Opens with the customer detail page shell, which this and the next two batches attach their actions to.

The page links to the card view at /kunden/[id]/karte
An unknown id renders a German not-found message, not a crash

userStories.title: Customer status transition state machine
userStories.description: As a developer, I need status transitions modelled as a state machine, so illegal transitions are impossible rather than merely unlikely. Source: tasks/prd-us-08-block-unblock-customer.md §US-08.1
acceptanceCriteria: src/domain/customer/status.ts defines Status = 'ACTIVE' | 'BLOCKED' | 'ARCHIVED' and transition(from, to)
Allowed: ACTIVE to BLOCKED, BLOCKED to ACTIVE, ACTIVE to ARCHIVED, BLOCKED to ARCHIVED
Refused with a typed IllegalStatusTransition error: any transition out of ARCHIVED, and any no-op transition
A transition to BLOCKED without a non-empty reason yields MissingAuditReason("customer.blocked") — the existing error in errors.ts, not a new class
Every transition pair, legal and illegal, has a test
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: src/domain/customer/status.ts adds transition(from,to,reason?) over the four allowed pairs; Status is aliased to the existing CustomerStatus in customer.ts (single source of truth). New typed IllegalStatusTransition error in errors.ts for any move out of ARCHIVED or any no-op; reason-less BLOCKED reuses MissingAuditReason("customer.blocked"). All 9 ordered pairs tested. 100% coverage held.

userStories.title: blockCustomer and unblockCustomer use cases
userStories.description: As a staff member, I want to pause a customer with a written reason and lift it later, so a customer can be paused without losing their number. Source: tasks/prd-us-08-block-unblock-customer.md §US-08.2
acceptanceCriteria: blockCustomer(deps, {customerId, reason}) sets status BLOCKED and stores the trimmed reason; an empty result rejects with MissingAuditReason
unblockCustomer(deps, {customerId}) returns the customer to ACTIVE and clears the reason
Neither use case changes the customer number, the card or any distribution record
Test asserts blocking does not free the slot — the taken-numbers query still includes it
Blocking an already-blocked customer and unblocking an active one both reject
Both write audit entries carrying the reason, with no actor field
Tested against hand-written fakes
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: block-customer.ts and unblock-customer.ts orchestrate transition() + a new CustomerRepository.setStatus(id,status,blockReason) port + audit. Block trims the reason, refuses whitespace via MissingAuditReason and illegal moves via IllegalStatusTransition; unblock reads the reason before clearing it so the audit why records the lifted block. Added blockReason to RegisteredCustomer and pulled the Prisma column + migration forward (a port method forces infra to compile and a reason needs a column) — US-004 keeps the invariant + slot-occupancy integration tests. Fake takenActiveNumbers now derives from live status so a block keeps the slot; all four customer fakes gained setStatus. 506 tests green, 100% on pure layers, build ok.

userStories.title: Block fields and slot-occupancy invariant
userStories.description: As a developer, I need blocked customers to occupy their slot exactly like active ones. Source: tasks/prd-us-08-block-unblock-customer.md §US-08.3
acceptanceCriteria: Customer.blockReason String? exists alongside status
An invariant test proves blockReason is non-null exactly when status is BLOCKED
Integration test proves the active-number unique index treats BLOCKED as occupying the slot; only ARCHIVED is exempt
Migration committed under prisma/migrations/
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: The blockReason column + migration landed in US-003; US-004 is the two proof tests. Added a setStatus invariant integration test proving (blockReason !== null) === (status === BLOCKED) is held across block → unblock and block → archive — it also pins that setStatus clears a stale reason, not just the status. Strengthened the slot-constraint tests: the active-number partial unique index refuses a BLOCKED row sharing an ACTIVE holder's number and refuses two BLOCKED on one number, while a BLOCKED and an ARCHIVED row may share a number (only ARCHIVED is exempt). No production change — the invariant is enforced by transition() + the use cases and the sole write path (setStatus writes both columns in one statement); the tests prove it. 511 tests green, 100% on pure layers.

userStories.title: Block and unblock UI
userStories.description: As a staff member, I want to block and unblock a customer and see the reason at the counter. Source: tasks/prd-us-08-block-unblock-customer.md §US-08.4
acceptanceCriteria: The customer detail page offers 'Sperren' with a required multi-line reason field; save is disabled until the reason is non-empty
A blocked customer's counter screen shows the reason verbatim and in full in the verdict banner — never truncated behind a 'more' link
'Sperre aufheben' is available from the customer detail page and asks for confirmation, showing the current reason before lifting
All user-facing strings come from src/i18n/de.ts
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Block/unblock UI on /kunden/[id]. New client component block-controls.tsx: an ACTIVE customer gets a 'Sperren' disclosure with a required multi-line textarea whose submit stays disabled until reason.trim() is non-empty (useState); a BLOCKED customer gets the current reason verbatim plus a confirming 'Sperre aufheben' disclosure that shows the reason being lifted before the button; an ARCHIVED customer gets nothing (no transition out of archived). actions.ts (blockCustomerAction/unblockCustomerAction) relays to the use cases, maps MissingAuditReason/IllegalStatusTransition to German, and revalidatePath's the record. The counter verdict banner already shows the reason verbatim/in full (US-04), so no change there. New i18n under customers.block. Browser check pending: no dev-browser skill/MCP this session.

userStories.title: E2E: blocked customer at the counter
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a Playwright spec proving a block is visible and reversible. Source: tasks/prd-us-08-block-unblock-customer.md §US-08.5
acceptanceCriteria: Spec blocks a customer with a reason, looks them up at the counter and asserts the reason is displayed and no serve action is offered
Spec asserts an empty reason cannot be submitted
Spec lifts the block and asserts the customer is servable again with the same customer number and the same card number
npm run test:e2e passes
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: tests/e2e/block.spec.ts (customer 241, RED/active, pinned to the RED distribution day 08.01.2026): blocks the household on /kunden/[id] with a multi-line reason, then reads it back verbatim/in full in the counter verdict banner with no serve-button offered; asserts an empty AND a whitespace-only reason leave block-submit disabled (FR-1); lifts the block via the confirming 'Sperre aufheben' and proves the household is CLEAR_TO_SERVE again on the same customer number and card (241k1). Surfaced a wiring gap: lookup-customer.ts hard-coded blockReason:null (a US-04-era TODO), so the counter always showed 'kein Grund hinterlegt' even for a reasoned block — now passes customer.blockReason through, with the lookup-customer 'blocks a blocked customer' unit test strengthened to assert {kind:'BLOCKED',reason:'gesperrt'}. E2E reuses a running server serving the OLD build (reuseExistingServer), so npm run build BEFORE npm run test:e2e when an app-layer change must reach the browser. Full e2e suite green (32 passed, 1 pre-existing skip); 511 unit tests, 100% on pure layers.
